allow: Bash(node -e "const t=''Every 14 days, a language dies. Amchi Konkani spoken by approximately 750000 Saraswat Brahmin diaspora members globally has no written script no digital presence and no speech recognition system placing it among the worlds most endangered languages. This study asks can community-driven data collection designed around how people already communicate motivate a geographically dispersed low-tech community to contribute language recordings and can those recordings combined with an existing Marathi AI model create working speech recognition for a language that has never had it? The independent variables were 1 how much of the AI to retrain fully versus partially and 2 whether to test it on speakers it had already encountered during training or on speakers it had never heard. The dependent variable was Word Error Rate WER the percentage of words transcribed incorrectly. Data collection was designed around observed community behavior elders already use WhatsApp daily so a sticker campaign was launched in which members created culturally expressive content that simultaneously contributed language data. Over two years 70 plus participants aged 16 to 80 contributed 675 recordings and 4876 dictionary entries 600 plus suggestions were submitted with 100 plus later corrected by other community members evidence of a self-organizing peer review system that emerged without prompting. Three training configurations were evaluated. Partially retraining the AI keeping its existing knowledge of Indian speech sounds intact and testing it on speakers it had never heard achieved 34.1 percent WER a 37.6 percent improvement over the fully retrained baseline 54.7 percent. Amchi Konkani and Marathi share speech sounds making Marathi a strong AI foundation. This methodology is peer-reviewed and accepted for archival publication and live demonstration at Speech Prosody 2026 University of Pennsylvania.''; console.log\(t.split\(/\\s+/\).length\)")
